attacks.attack: One-click final assets is exactly the sentence that ends up in a layoff deck. If the tool did that, you wouldn't need us. It doesn't, and saying it makes every artist on the team your enemy.

attacks.attack: Production-ready on a flagship title means it passes art review. Nothing generated has passed ours. Overclaim it and the guild has its next post.

stress.rewrite: Base meshes for props and background assets in minutes, ready for your team to finish in Blender or the engine. 37 Interactive cut high-poly work by 30 to 40%.
stress.rewrite_rationale: Drops 'production-ready' and 'one-click', which every critic attacked, scopes the promise to the hybrid pipeline with artists finishing the work, and uses the one cleanup-related proof point in the MRD.

transcript.text: Meshy gives your team base meshes in minutes, inside your existing pipeline, so you can spend your time on the work that matters.
The work that matters. So the props don't? Half my job is props. When a studio says AI will save time, I hear that they'll need fewer of us. And I'd want to know what your model was trained on.

Fair. Meshy is trained only on licensed data, and your studio can switch off training on anything you make. You decide what it touches. Most teams start with background props and keep hero assets by hand.

Licensed is a word every vendor uses. If I could see where the data came from, and my lead put in writing that we pick what goes to the tool, I'd try it on crates and barrels. Not on anything with my name on it.
That's how we'd run the pilot: your team picks the asset list, and there's a free certification so you're the one who knows the tool best.

The certification is interesting, actually. If the studio uses this anyway, I'd rather be the one who knows it. But the first 500k-triangle crate I have to retopologize, I'm out, and I'll be the one telling the team whether it's worth it.

brief.summary: Meshy is an AI 3D generation platform. It turns a sketch, photo or prompt into a textured, rigged, print-ready model in about a minute, sends it into Blender, Unity, Unreal or a slicer, and offers an API, a shared studio workspace and enterprise controls. The SMB push adds a free Meshy Certified program and an AI outreach agent, Myko.
brief.target: Net-new SMB customers across four equally weighted segments: amateurs, individual pros and startups (including print and e-commerce shops), SMB game studios of 10 to 200 people, and large studios and publishers.
brief.proposition: Base meshes in minutes, finished in your tools, and every model stays yours.
brief.tone: Plain, specific and respectful of craft. Talk like a technical artist who has shipped games, not like an AI company. Confident, never hyped. No exclamation marks.
mandatories: Never imply replacing artists, cutting headcount or beating a human modeler.
Promise a hybrid pipeline, never one-click final assets.
Only use claims with proof in the MRD; the blind test, user counts and the 4.7 rating stay out.
Include at least one trust line in every direction: ownership, private by default, or opt out of training.
Never disparage Tripo, Rodin or Hunyuan3D by name.

features.name: Print-ready export
features.description: Watertight, slicer-ready models sent straight to Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer.

features.name: Engine and DCC plugins
features.description: Send models into Blender, Unity, Unreal, Godot, Maya and Roblox Studio.

features.name: API and MCP for agents
features.description: Generate and refine from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or a custom pipeline.

features.name: Studio workspace
features.description: Shared seats and credits, private by default, with an admin switch to opt out of model training.

features.name: Enterprise controls
features.description: SAML SSO, SOC 2 and ISO 27001, customer-set retention, and training exclusion by contract.

features.name: Meshy Certified program
features.description: A free 60 to 90 minute course and practical exam; agencies and print shops with two certified staff become Certified Partners.
